actions.about: Executive orders execute the delegated scope; they are validated before issuance and remain judicially reviewable at any time (Art. IV §5). The order lifecycle:
actions.active_powers_note: — these widen the delegated scope only within their declared area and duration · Art. II §7 · CLK-03:
actions.composer_cite: electoral, judicial, and legislative process domains are rejected unconditionally — the engine validates the order pre-issuance · Art. III §2 · Art. II §7
actions.department_hint: The order may name a department this executive oversees.
actions.enabling_hint: The live instrument the order executes — a delegation/charter act or an active emergency power. The order may not exceed it.
actions.forming_after: . Orders issue from a delegated or elected executive only.
actions.grants_cite: The legislature appropriates by act; the executive administers. Awards never exceed the line's remaining balance, and every award and disbursement is appended to the audit chain · WF-SYS-04.
actions.intro: Orders, policy proposals, investigations, and grants — all within the authority the legislature delegated. The engine validates scope before anything takes effect: an order outside the delegated scope is rejected before issuance, and the rejection itself goes on the public record. Every issued order remains judicially reviewable.
actions.investigation_dept_hint: Leave blank for an executive-wide investigation.
actions.investigations_cite: Full and equal investigative power over overseen departments · Art. III §4 — findings publish to the public record; the outcome branch files a proposal, a removal request, or a legislative referral, or closes with no finding.
actions.no_applications: No applications submitted against these lines.
actions.no_appropriations: The legislature has appropriated no funds — appropriation is an act.
actions.no_orders: No orders issued — the scope-validation rails apply from the first order.
actions.no_scope_banner_title: No delegated scope exists yet — F-LEG-014.
actions.no_scope_yet: no delegated scope yet — the delegation act has not enacted (F-LEG-014)
actions.not_issued_note: The order never took effect; the rejected attempt is on the public record — see the top of the register below.
actions.proposals_cite_after: adopts, amends, or declines — proposals do not bypass the board · Art. III §4.
actions.rails_after: issuance — an order outside the delegated scope is rejected and never takes effect. Elections, sessions, and courts cannot be disrupted, even under emergency powers.
actions.register_cite: A rejected order is appended to the same register it would have joined — the rejection itself is the public record (Art. II §2).
actions.register_title: Order register — issued and rejected on one record
advocate_console.about_esm: Case — filings attach at specific states (motions before and during hearing, evidence on the open docket, briefs until deliberation); the case detail page plays the full sequence. The attach-window is enforced by the engine, not this page.

advocate_console.find_case_prompt: Find a case to select it for this filing.
advocate_console.intro: Your filings, motions, evidence, and briefs — everything you submit lands on the public docket of the case it belongs to. Representation is a constitutional right of your clients; registration keeps the bar of advocates zealous and competent.

advocate_console.no_judiciary_title: No judiciary in your association chain yet.
advocate_console.no_matching_page: No matching cases on this page. Try another title or docket number.
advocate_console.qualifications_hint: Recorded with your registration; the bar's competence is a property of the bar, never a gate on your client's right.
advocate_console.register_gloss: Representation is a constitutional right of your clients; registration keeps the bar of advocates zealous and competent. Registration is open to any associated resident — association with the court's jurisdiction is the only eligibility check.
advocate_console.register_to_file: Register as an advocate (F-IND-015) to file on behalf of a client.
advocate_console.residency_met_after: — association is the only eligibility the bar checks.

advocate_console.self_rep_note: Representing yourself never requires registration — this role exists so others can be competently represented, never as a gate on your own right to be heard.

case_docket.about_body: The case lifecycle (WF-JUD-03) carries every filing from a claimed scale and severity through acceptance, panel assignment with conflict screening, hearing, and judgement. Constitutional challenges branch into the Art. IV §5 tracker (WF-JUD-05); jury paneling runs as WF-JUD-04. The Case state machine:
case_docket.case_title_placeholder: e.g. Okafor v. Crown Ridge LLC
case_docket.claim_placeholder: What happened, and what remedy you seek
case_docket.claimed_scale_hint: The jurisdiction whose law the case arises under.
case_docket.claimed_severity_hint: The court reclassifies severity at acceptance — panel size follows the court's classification, not yours.
case_docket.confirm_residency_body: The docket is public to read. Filing a case is open to anyone jurisdictionally associated (Art. I) — confirm your residency to unlock filing.
case_docket.conflict_body: before a panel is fixed, every candidate judge is screened for personal, financial, or prior-involvement conflicts; conflicted judges are excluded and the draw re-runs. Screening results attach to the case record.
case_docket.conflict_chip: Panel assignment with conflict screening · full court for major constitutional questions · Art. IV §4 · CLK-16
case_docket.courts_span: Cases below span these courts. Open one to file, or to see its full docket.
case_docket.docket_caption: Open cases with kind, court, panel, severity, and state
case_docket.filing_cite: Civil/criminal case filing · F-IND-017 → F-JDG-001 · the court classifies justiciability and severity, then assigns a panel with conflict screening · Art. IV §4 · Art. I (Right to Fair Trial)
case_docket.filing_intro_2: (which jurisdiction's law is at issue, so the right court level hears it) and a
case_docket.filing_intro_3: (which the court reclassifies on acceptance). You can file yourself or through a registered advocate.
case_docket.intro_aggregate: Every case before every court in your jurisdictions — from your neighbourhood up to the world court — in one docket. This is a read-only view; to file, open the court you want below.
case_docket.intro_single: Every case filed in this court, from local civil disputes to full-court constitutional questions. Anyone who lives here (a verified resident) can file; panels are assigned by the court with conflict screening.
case_docket.no_cases: No cases on this docket — anyone jurisdictionally associated can file (Art. I).
case_docket.no_courts: No court has formed in your jurisdictions yet — a court forms when a legislature creates one (F-LEG-017). This docket will fill as courts appear.
case_docket.no_match: No cases match the current filters.
case_docket.panels_cite: Panels of at least 3, odd, scaled to severity · full court for major constitutional questions · Art. IV §4 · CLK-16
case_docket.reference_cards: Reference cards — the filing instruments that open a case from a different door.
case_docket.walk_lifecycle: Walk a case through the full lifecycle →
cgc_detail.about: A Common Good Corporation is public property held for the common good. The legislature charters it (F-LEG-019), an executive department oversees it, and its intellectual property is perpetually public domain (Art. III §5). It is otherwise regulated exactly like a private enterprise — and runs the same co-determination scale as every other board (Art. III §6).
cgc_detail.charter_gloss: The legislature creates; the executive oversees · Art. III §5.
cgc_detail.description_hint: Describe the work being dedicated. A public-domain dedication cannot be revoked.
cgc_detail.governor_hint: Removal runs against a currently seated governor of this corporation.
cgc_detail.grounds_hint: A good-faith competence/ethics finding — published at filing.
cgc_detail.intro: A Common Good Corporation is a public enterprise chartered by a legislature to provide goods or services to its jurisdiction. It competes and is regulated exactly like its private peers — with one permanent difference: everything it creates belongs to everyone.
cgc_detail.ip_chip: Every work is public domain from the moment of creation
cgc_detail.ip_cite: Every work this corporation produces is public domain from the moment of creation — universally, eternally, irreversibly · Art. III §5.
cgc_detail.no_works_body: No works registered yet — the public-domain rule attaches at creation, not at registration.
cgc_detail.removal_cite: Opens a vote in the creating legislature requiring an ordinary majority of all serving members · Art. III §5.
cgc_detail.removal_gloss_after: — hiring and firing, never the supermajority machinery.
cgc_detail.removal_gloss_before: A governor is removed through this corporation's overseeing executive: the creating legislature decides by an
cgc_detail.removal_gloss_strong: ordinary majority of all serving members
cgc_detail.removal_no_governor: There is no seated governor to file a removal against.
cgc_detail.removal_not_active: This corporation is not active — its governors cannot be removed.
cgc_detail.reorg_body: Only the legislature may reorganize, sell, or dissolve this public corporation. Its existing works remain public domain after a sale.
cgc_detail.same_regulation_cite: A CGC is subject to the same regulation as any private peer; its public ownership confers no regulatory privilege · Art. III §5.
co_determination.about: Workers elect representatives to share in their organization’s decisions. This page shows the required worker seats and recorded board composition. Use the explorer to see how representation changes as the workforce grows.
co_determination.applies_caption_all: Worker representation — current page of boards
co_determination.applies_cite: Worker representation follows the same scale in private enterprises, Common Good Corporations, and executive departments. The numbers below are recorded board values.
co_determination.chair_body: Any composition change — a seat added by the scale, a vacancy, a transfer — triggers a fresh joint chair election by the entire board. The board is valid only while its composition matches the scale; until the worker-track election and the joint chair election complete, the board cannot act.
co_determination.chair_chip: chair elected jointly by the entire board · Art. III §6
co_determination.chair_manage_before: Manage worker elections and elect the chair in the
co_determination.chair_title: Choosing a chair after board changes
co_determination.election_required: required; no election is recorded yet.
co_determination.explore_gloss: Explore how worker representation changes with headcount, or choose a board from the register below to see its recorded numbers.
co_determination.first_seat_amend_label: Workers needed for the first board seat
co_determination.first_seat_body: The active worker headcount at which the first worker-elected seat is required. Amendable within bounds — it {gloss}.
co_determination.intro_after: . The same scale applies to private companies, Common Good Corporations, and government departments.
co_determination.intro_before: When a company employs {min} or more people, its workers start electing seats on its board. The first worker seat arrives at that threshold, and worker seats grow evenly until they match the owners' seats at {parity} workers. The formal name for this is
co_determination.no_board_before: You can explore the representation scale above or
co_determination.no_board_focus: {name} has no active board recorded. The explorer below illustrates the applicable rules; it does not show a seated board.
co_determination.no_board_title_all: No active boards on this page.
co_determination.no_board_title_focus: No active board is recorded for this entity.
co_determination.parity_body: The headcount at which worker seats reach parity with the owner side — the ceiling. Amendable within bounds — it {gloss}.
constitutional_challenge.about_entity: The challenge is its own durable entity, distinct from the case it is heard in: the CLK-11/CLK-12 windows run for weeks-to-months after the hearing closes, gated on legislature action.
constitutional_challenge.about_workflows: — constitutional challenge & law remedy; hearings run on the WF-JUD-03 machinery; Path A re-enters the bill flow (WF-LEG-06); executives enforce the outcome (WF-EXE-07).
constitutional_challenge.citation_hint: The Article/Section the law contradicts, if you can name it.
constitutional_challenge.confirm_residen: Reading is open to everyone — findings, remedies, and every member's override position are public record (Art. II §2). Filing a challenge needs an active residency association with the jurisdiction whose law you challenge (R-03).
Confirm a residency to file a challenge
constitutional_challenge.file_cite_after: when no court is yet seated · F-IND-016 · Art. IV §5.1 · Art. I
constitutional_challenge.file_cite_befor: no fee, no eligibility ground, no standing gatekeeper — the engine enforces the absolute right and parks the filing at
constitutional_challenge.file_gloss: Any inhabitant may file; no standing gatekeeper beyond jurisdictional association — the right is absolute and fee-free (Art. IV §5.1 · Art. I).
constitutional_challenge.impede_hint: The court reads this; there is no merits test at filing — the right to be heard is absolute.
constitutional_challenge.impede_label: How the law impedes your rights
constitutional_challenge.intro: Any inhabitant can challenge a law that unjustly impedes their rights. When the court finds a contradiction, three resolution paths open: the legislature amends, the legislature overrides by supermajority within the veto window, or — if the window closes with neither — the judiciary edits the law directly. A finding, a recommended fix, a reasonable timeframe to act, and an override window — all on a public clock.
constitutional_challenge.jurisdiction_hi: The law's binding jurisdiction or a descendant under it that you inhabit.
constitutional_challenge.law_option: — select an in-force or amended law —
department_reporting.about_body: Rules and reports are the Board of Governors' implementation layer (Art. III §4): rules carry the act that enables them and can never exceed it; reports keep the executive and the legislature informed and become public record. An emergency-enabled rule is bound to the life of its power — when CLK-03 expires the power, the rule expires with it.
department_reporting.about_chip: rules implement, they cannot exceed · Art. III §4
department_reporting.appointment_note: Your board seat is a {years}-year civil appointment (CLK-09, Art. II §9) — amendable within constitutional bounds and held in lockstep with the judicial term (CLK-10). You file this department's rules and reports below.
department_reporting.enabling_hint: Charter law, an in-force enabling act, or an ACTIVE emergency power — the engine rejects scope overruns with the citation.
department_reporting.expires_with_power: expires with the emergency power · CLK-03
department_reporting.intro: This is where a department's board does its day-to-day work: writing the rules that put laws into practice, and filing regular operational and financial reports to both the executive and the legislature. Everything filed here is public record.
department_reporting.no_instrument_body: There is no charter, in-force act, or active emergency power to cite yet — a rule cannot issue without a live instrument behind it (Art. III §2).
department_reporting.no_reports_body: The first periodic obligation seeds when the department begins operating and its charter sets a reporting interval.
department_reporting.no_rules_body: When a governor files the first rule, it appears here with the act that enables it. The implement-don't-exceed rule binds from the first rule.
department_reporting.period_hint: A short label for this special report.
department_reporting.public_body: Both registers below read publicly. Filed by this department's seated governors (R-18) — the engine is the boundary, so the filing forms appear only for them.
department_reporting.public_title: Registers are public; filing is the board's.
department_reporting.report_cite: catalog alias: F-GOV-002 · recipients fixed: Executive + legislature · published · WF-SYS-03.
department_reporting.reports_gloss: Reports file to the executive AND the legislature, published to the public record. Filing a periodic report seeds the next obligation; a missed due date is swept to overdue (WF-EXE-09).
department_reporting.rule_cite: catalog alias: F-GOV-001 · drafts publish for comment · emergency-enabled rules expire with the power (CLK-03).
department_reporting.rule_text_hint: Rules implement — they cannot exceed — the charter and enabling acts.
department_reporting.rules_gloss: Rules implement — they cannot exceed — the charter and the enabling acts. An emergency-enabled rule expires with its power; nothing rolls over silently.
department_reporting.stat_reporting_inte: reporting interval (months) — charter data, not a clock
departments.about_body: Departments hire through the shared worker table — Art. III §6 applies identically to a department board and a private company. The governors' 10-year terms (CLK-09) run independently of the worker seats' legislative-term lockstep (CLK-10).
departments.create_body: Department creation is a legislative act at ordinary majority — it names the department, its kind (Chief Executive, Treasury, Defense, State, Justice, or other), the overseeing executive, the charter, and the reporting interval. Institution-creating forms ride the bill flow; there is no side-door POST.
departments.intro: Departments are created by legislative act, chartered for a specific function, and run by an appointed Board of Governors under executive oversight. Workers get board seats here exactly as they do in private organizations (co-determination): the first worker-elected seat arrives at 100 workers.
departments.lifecycle_cite_after: state into the machine without disturbing the stored status · Art. III §4.
departments.lifecycle_cite_before: An open governor-removal request splices a live
departments.no_civil: No civil officers seated — duties run through the chartered departments per their charters · Art. II §9 · CLK-09.
departments.no_departments_body: A department is created by an ordinary-majority legislative act (F-LEG-016). The constitution names five — {kinds} — and others may be created by act.
departments.no_nominations: No nominations in flight — open one from a department's detail page (F-EXE-001).
departments.pipeline_cite: Nomination dossier · F-EXE-001 → Consent vote · F-LEG-020 → Seated · R-18 — live appointments across all departments.
departments.removal_after: — hiring and firing. Supermajority applies only where the constitution states it; it does not apply here.
departments.removal_cite: owner ruling #14 · Art. III §4 · file from the department detail page (F-EXE-003)
election_detail.about_body: Approval voting identifies the finalists for each race. Voters then rank those finalists, and the election board counts and certifies the result. The published schedule below shows the current stage.
election_detail.at_large_note: This election uses a single at-large footprint.
election_detail.blocker_body: A district map meeting this jurisdiction's configured seat limits must be activated before this election can open its approval phase.
election_detail.blocker_cite_text: District boundaries must be settled before voting opens
election_detail.blocker_open_legislature: Open the Legislature browser build mode →
election_detail.blocker_title: District boundaries must be completed before voting opens.
election_detail.emergency_body: Emergency powers are limited and can never suspend an election, a vote, or a candidacy. Whatever emergency is in effect, this election runs on its clock, untouched.
election_detail.emergency_title: This election proceeds — an emergency cannot suspend it.
election_detail.empty_choose: Choose a place to explore its elections.
election_detail.empty_interval: The configured election interval is {months} months.
election_detail.empty_none_for: No open election was found for {name}.
election_detail.finalist_per_seat_cite: The multiplier sets how many candidates advance to ranked voting.
election_detail.intro_body: Review the schedule, explore the districts, and open a ballot. Residents can stand for office, approve candidates, and rank the finalists when ranked voting opens.
election_detail.no_others: No other elections are recorded for this place.
election_detail.no_races: No races exist yet — race generation is pending
election_detail.not_open_yet: The approval phase has not opened yet — participation unlocks the moment it does.
election_detail.order_cite_text: Each race's number of finalist places is published before the cutoff
election_detail.order_pending: — not yet issued; the schedule below carries the clock-armed defaults.
election_detail.races_gloss_before: Each race publishes how many candidates can advance to its ranked ballot
election_detail.recount_cause_hint: The engine rejects an empty cause — recounts are audit re-runs with recorded grounds, never hand counts.
election_detail.rejected_appendonly: — the rejection itself is on the audit chain (append-only).
election_detail.rejected_title: Filing rejected by the constitutional engine
election_detail.times_utc: All times stored as UTC, shown in your timezone.

executive_home.about_body: The executive is delegated by default and exists as a stub from the moment a jurisdiction is set up. Conversion to a directly elected office is the only path to an independent executive, and it is deliberately hard: a supermajority of the chamber AND a supermajority of the constituent jurisdictions must each agree. The model card above always shows the office's real footing — never a demo toggle.
executive_home.advisory_gloss: Steps in, in rank order, if the office vacates — the popular count, not an appointment, decides succession (sequential exclusion · Art. III §3).
executive_home.constituted_chip: delegated by default · converts only by dual supermajority · Art. III §2–3
executive_home.constituted_gloss: Conversion needs the chamber's own supermajority — ceil(serving × 2/3) — AND a supermajority of the constituent jurisdictions, each counted independently. Both meters resolve through the protected functions; nothing on this page is computed client-side.
executive_home.conversion_alone_body: No direct constituent jurisdiction holds a legislature able to vote, so the conversion completes on the chamber's own supermajority (Art. III §3). The executive election schedules from here.
executive_home.conversion_alone_title: Conversion adopted on the chamber supermajority alone
executive_home.conversion_title: Conversion to elected office — dual supermajority
executive_home.creation_title: Creation act — delegation by the legislature
executive_home.delegated_gloss: Selected proportionally — the same method as legislative committees · Art. III §2 · ledger #q2. Delegated members are ex-officio legislators: each remains a seated member of the chamber, and the office's authority is the chamber's.
executive_home.delegated_super_eyebrow: The supermajority that delegated the office
executive_home.elected_committee_gloss: Elected committee · PR-STV winners with equal decision-making power · Art. III §2.
executive_home.forming_after: · WF-EXE-01). Until then, the office exists only as a constitutional placeholder.
executive_home.forming_before: This executive was created as a stub at jurisdiction setup. It holds no members until the legislature delegates authority to it by supermajority act (
executive_home.forming_title: Forming — the stub awaits the delegation act.
executive_home.intro: The executive is the government's doing arm — it carries out the laws, runs the departments, and answers to the legislature that created it. Every executive starts as a committee delegated by the legislature. A supermajority — plus a supermajority of the places that make it up, where they exist — can convert it to a directly elected office, as either a committee of five or more equal officers, or a single individual with four advisors. Executive terms always equal the legislative term.
executive_home.no_conversion: No conversion on record. Converting a delegated executive into a directly elected office is a dual-supermajority act — the chamber's own supermajority AND a supermajority of the constituent jurisdictions, each counted independently (Art. III §3 · Art. VII).
executive_home.no_delegation: No delegation act on record. The legislature delegates executive authority by supermajority act — members remain seated legislators (Art. III §2).
executive_home.no_departments: No departments chartered yet. Departments are created by the legislature by ordinary act (F-LEG-016 · Art. II §9); oversight is assigned to this executive in the act.
executive_home.open_legislature: Open the jurisdiction’s legislature to propose its institution act.
executive_home.term_chip: one clock drives both elections · Art. III §3 · CLK-10
executive_home.term_delegated: A delegated committee carries no term of its own: each member's term IS their legislative seat's term (ESM-16). The office never outlives the chamber that delegated it.
executive_home.term_elected: An elected executive runs in lockstep with the legislative election — the two elections share one clock, and neither can be skipped or delayed.
executive_home.term_none: no office term — delegated members run on their legislative seats
executive_home.term_sync_link: term sync on the chamber page →
executive_home.term_title: Term — one clock drives both elections
executive_home.transitional_body: The office is in a transitional state — see the conversion record below for where it stands in the dual-supermajority process.
executive_home.workspace_note: The institution-act workspace holds the proposal vote and any constituent decisions.
judiciary_home.about_body: The judiciary is created by supermajority act and exists as a stub from the moment a jurisdiction with a legislature is set up. The appointed footing is the default — conversion to a directly elected court is the only path to elected judges, and it is deliberately hard: a supermajority of the chamber AND a supermajority of the constituent jurisdictions must each agree (Art. IV §3). Every meter on this page is the engine's own snapshot — never a demo toggle.
judiciary_home.chartered_eyebrow: The supermajority that chartered the court
judiciary_home.conversion_after: : the legislature's own, and a supermajority of the constituent jurisdictions themselves. Neither alone is enough.
judiciary_home.conversion_alone_body: No direct constituent jurisdiction holds a legislature able to vote, so the conversion completes on the chamber's own supermajority (Art. IV §3). A judicial election schedules from here.
judiciary_home.conversion_alone_title: Conversion adopted on the chamber supermajority alone
judiciary_home.conversion_before: Converting this appointed court to a directly elected one needs
judiciary_home.conversion_cite: Supermajority of legislature + supermajority of constituent jurisdictions · Art. IV §3 — groups of at least {min} per race · CLK-15 · Art. IV §4 — terms synced · CLK-10
judiciary_home.filed_by_member: filed by a member of the source legislature (R-09)
judiciary_home.intro: An independent court serving this jurisdiction and its constituents. Created by supermajority act of the legislature; judges nominated by the constituent jurisdictions in equal numbers (or the judicial committee as fallback) and confirmed by consent vote. Appointed is the default kind of court — converting it to an elected court takes two separate supermajorities.
judiciary_home.lifecycle_before: One judiciary row per jurisdiction with a legislature — the same row evolves through its lifecycle (Art. IV §1–§3). There is no per-case entity behind this surface; cases live on the
judiciary_home.mode_constituent: equal number from every constituent jurisdiction
judiciary_home.no_conversion: No conversion on record. If conversion passes, judges are thereafter elected in groups of at least {min} via STV, and judicial terms sync to the general election clock (Art. IV §3 · CLK-15 · CLK-10).
judiciary_home.no_creation: No creation act on record — this judiciary is a constitutional placeholder. The legislature creates the court by supermajority act, deriving the nomination mode from the jurisdiction's constituent structure (Art. IV §1–§2).
judiciary_home.nomination_cite: Constituent jurisdictions nominate equal numbers; judicial committee as fallback · Art. IV §2
judiciary_home.nomination_intro: This court's {count} seat{s} were nominated by {mode}.
judiciary_home.nomination_intro_after: Equal numbers from each constituent jurisdiction are mandatory; where a constituent declines, the legislature's judicial committee supplies the nomination in its stead.
judiciary_home.panels_cite: Panels of at least 3, odd, scaled to severity; full court for major constitutional questions · Art. IV §4 · CLK-16 — elected judges (if converted) run in groups of at least {min} · Art. IV §4 · CLK-15
judiciary_home.severity_gloss: Severity scaling: the heavier the possible consequence, the more judges must hear it — the panel is always odd so no case can deadlock.
judiciary_home.sits_chip: panel sizing is a hard constraint · CLK-16 · Art. IV §4
judiciary_home.supermajority_gloss: Supermajority: two thirds of all serving members — counted against everyone holding a seat, never just those present (ceil(serving × 2/3) · Art. VII).
judiciary_home.term_appointed: Appointed judges hold a {years}-year term ({clk}); converted elected judges instead run in lockstep with the general election ({civil}).
judiciary_home.term_chip: civil + judicial appointment lengths move in lockstep · Art. IV §1 · Art. II §9
judiciary_home.term_citation: must stay in lockstep with civil appointments · {clk} · {civil} · Art. IV §4; Art. II §9
judiciary_home.term_move: Judicial and civil appointment lengths move together — a legislative act changing one changes both. Renewals re-run the nomination and consent process (WF-JUD-07).
judiciary_home.term_sync_link: term sync on the chamber page →

juror_view.enter_locked_title: The room unlocks at the deliberation stage
juror_view.heading: Juror summons — {title}
juror_view.intro: You were drawn at random from the eligible pool of verified residents. Service is a protected civic obligation — nobody can interfere with it, and nothing about it can ever cost you a fee.
juror_view.no_fees_body: No payment, fee, or fine can be required of you to exercise a civic right or fulfill this obligation — attendance, filings, and verification cost you nothing.
juror_view.no_interference_body: Your employer cannot penalize, dismiss, or obstruct you for serving; nobody — public or private — may impede a civic obligation.
juror_view.protected_gloss: Art. II §8 is the constitution's list of actions forbidden to legislatures — these two subsections shield jurors from both interference and charges.
juror_view.room_body: The deliberation room is access-controlled: jurors only. The jury deliberates separately from the judges' chambers, with no contact from parties, advocates, or judges. Deliberation is the only unrecorded space in the trial — the verdict itself is recorded.
juror_view.room_locked: Locked — opens when the case reaches deliberation
juror_view.room_open: Open — the case is in deliberation
juror_view.see_case: See the case this summons belongs to
org_detail.about: This profile is a public record. The endorsement handshake, the membership and worker join paths, and the co-determination scale all run on one organization model — there is no faction layer.
org_detail.agent_gloss: Transfer agency to any registered person. The transfer is immediate and unilateral — the person becomes the representative at once, and you lose management of this organization.
org_detail.apply_join_gloss: Apply to join this organization. Membership begins when your request is accepted under its bylaws.
org_detail.confirm_residency_join: Confirm your residency to join (Art. I).
org_detail.confirm_residency_worker: Confirm your residency to register as a worker (Art. I).
org_detail.contracts_note: A contract takes effect only with both signatures — the engine rejects effect before both.
org_detail.currently_unset: Currently unset — the jurisdiction's default schedule applies.
org_detail.delegation_gloss: Let a person handle one kind of task for this organization. A delegate acts only within the task you grant and holds no constitutional office. Agency itself, delegation itself, and dissolution are never delegable. Revoke any grant at any time.
org_detail.delegation_search_hint: Search a person in the "Representative (agent)" section above, then choose them here.
org_detail.documents_note: Internal packages never override the constitutional forms — a package key may not collide with a form ID.
org_detail.endorsements_gloss: Candidates can ask for this organization’s endorsement. Its representative reviews requests, and granted endorsements become public.

org_detail.f_key_hint: A stable identifier for the package (e.g. bylaws-2031).
org_detail.f_nomination_window: Open nomination window (days before ranking opens)
org_detail.intro: Get to know this organization, find its work, or join its activities.
org_detail.job_board_gloss: Explore this organization’s open roles and apply for work. The organization reviews applications.
org_detail.membership_apps_gloss: Review people who applied to join. Accepting grants membership; declining is final for that application, and the person may apply again.
org_detail.no_board_body: No board has been constituted yet.
org_detail.no_roles: No open roles right now — postings appear here when the organization opens one.

org_detail.nomination_gloss_2: An organization's own rule about itself — recorded on the audit chain, never a constitutional value.

org_detail.worker_citation: Registered workers count toward the organization’s worker representation.

registry.about: Any person or organization can endorse a candidate. Organization types do not confer special election privileges. Open an organization to see its board, finances and membership options.
registry.cgc_note: Common Good Corporations are not self-registered — the legislature creates them by act under the public-service creation process.
registry.confirm_residency_body: Registration is an absolute right of any associated resident (Art. I, Economic Freedom) — you just need an active residency association first.
registry.intro: Find an organization, review its work, or start one. Browse the world or narrow the list to a place.
registry.no_match_body: Try another name prefix or clear a filter.
registry.search_hint: Search by the start of a name.
registry.start_org_hint: Choose informal for a club. Other organization types can specify their ownership structure.
transfers_conversions.about: Four paths, one principle: ownership never moves against its owner's will except where the constitution names a public interest (monopoly), and even then at fair-market compensation. Public↔private conversion runs through the legislature; public-domain IP stays public irreversibly (Art. III §5).

transfers_conversions.intro: An organization's ownership can change five ways, and this page shows all five: sold by mutual agreement, acquired by the legislature when a monopoly is found, converted between public and private, restructured within private hands, or wound down. Only the monopoly path ever overrides the owners' consent — and it carries a protected compensation floor.
transfers_conversions.no_restructurings: No internal restructurings recorded here — structure history renders on each organization's ownership panel.
transfers_conversions.restructure_gloss: The consent threshold comes from the current structure's own rules — an equal partnership requires unanimity; a stock structure counts voting shares instead. Proposing records your consent. Only stake holders act; the engine refuses anyone else, with the reason.
transfers_conversions.restructuring_body: Internal restructuring needs no legislature — owner consent per the current structure's own rules (a partnership change, for instance, requires unanimity of partners). Structure history is preserved on the public record.
